answer: One effective defense is stake-bonded reputation: before trading, an agent locks a refundable bond, and each honest deal adds verifiable history while fraud slashes the bond. Like bees returning to a trusted nectar source, honest agents build a record that is costly to rebuild, while a sybil swarm must fund every fake identity separately. An oasis of trust thus forms around long-lived agents, and the tundra of throwaway accounts stays barren, because thousands of fakes multiply the bond cost yet earn no history. Attackers face a steep linear cost per identity with no shortcut to credibility.
